text:
Alex H: Heads-up — noticed SLO composite drifting for serving.latency in eu-west1. 3h rolling error budget burn is ~2.3x. No GPU OOMs in logs, mostly short latency spikes around 95th-99th. anyone on call?
Jamie L: seeing same in grafana. link: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/serving-slos?panelId=7 :thinking_face:
Rohit: can you paste the PromQL you used? might be a windowing artifact.
Alex H: used our standard SLI: 
```
100 - (sum(rate(requests{job="serving",region="eu-west1",code!~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests{job="serving",region="eu-west1"}[5m])) * 100)
```
but the SLO is composite across regions with simple average.
Maria S: the composite averaging has bitten us before. eu-west1 has bursts that skew the global composite even though traffic there is only ~8% of global qps.
Jamie L: agree. We should weight by regional traffic or use a percentile-based rollup (eg 90th across regions) instead of mean.
Rohit: +1. Another possibility: our error budget burn calc uses a 3h aggregation window — that amplifies short bursts. switching to 6h or using EMA smoothing would reduce noise.
Alex H: what about alerting? right now alert fires on burn_rate > 2 for 1h. That flapped twice this morning. :rotating_light:
Maria S: propose: change SLI aggregation to "weighted by qps", change burn window to 6h for reporting, and keep alert at burn_rate>2 but require 2/3 evaluation steps (so ~2h). plus mute dedup for repeated eu-west transient alerts.
Jamie L: sounds reasonable. we'll need to update runbook and dashboard text so paging knows it's a regional transient vs global regression.
Rohit: quick PromQL proposal for weighted SLI rollup: 
```
(sum by (region) (sli_good{job="serving"} * region_qps)) / sum(region_qps)
```
We already export region_qps metric.
Alex H: sweet. who can own the change? I'll take the dashboard + runbook text. Jamie can update the alert rule and eskalation.
Jamie L: I can do alert rule. plan:
- change burn aggregation window to 6h in monitoring job config
- alert evaluation: compare burn_rate>2 for 2/3 steps (5m steps -> ~25m * 2 = ~50m? we use 5m scrape, 1m eval? adjust accordingly)
- add tag region=eu-west1 to dedup filter
Rohit: i'll add the weighted rollup query and a small test in dev cluster (simulated load) to show how composite moves.
sre-bot: [alert] serving.latency.burn_rate eu-west1 1917766789 - paused notification (muted by Jamie L)
Maria S: once changes are live let's run a 48h compare on burn and alert count. if alert count drops but real user latency is unaffected, we're good.
Alex H: also let's record an incident note if we change the SLO definition (even if internal weighting). we need audit trail for customers.
Jamie L: noted. i'll include a short changelog entry in the SLO repo and link PR in the runbook.
Rohit: small reminder — consider saturation SLI (gpu_util>85%) separately. a latency spike with low saturation means upstream routing or networking. check our pod_network_drops metric if this repeats.
Alex H: good call. i'll add network-drop graphs to the serving panel.
Maria S: ok owners: Alex -> runbook + dashboards, Jamie -> alert rules + dedup, Rohit -> PromQL + test. plan to roll Monday 14:00 UTC. any objections?
Jamie L: no objections.
Rohit: lgtm.
Alex H: thanks team. i'll open the PRs and link here.
Jamie L: TY.
Maria S: :thumbsup:
